title: HC orders Tamil Nadu Police to deny permission for protests ‘targeting’ judges

ai.summary: The Madras High Court ordered Tamil Nadu Police to deny protest permits targeting judges and disperse gatherings that personally attack judges, following protests against a Supreme Court ruling on religious conversion and reservations.

facts.claim: The Madras High Court directed Tamil Nadu Police to deny permission for protests against judges
facts.quote: The Madras High Court on Friday directed the Tamil Nadu Police to deny permission for protests against judges and to immediately disperse any gatherings where personal attacks are made on a judge.

facts.claim: The court ruled that a 'blanket order' banning all public discussions or peaceful gatherings concerning court rulings would go too far
facts.quote: The court ruled that a "blanket order" banning all public discussions or peaceful gatherings concerning court rulings "would go too far".

facts.claim: The court directed state police to consider protest applications on a case-by-case basis for judicial decisions
facts.quote: The bench directed state police and district administrations to consider applications for protests pertaining to judicial decisions on a case-by-case basis.

facts.claim: The court said no permission shall be granted for gatherings aiming to personally target, defame or intimidate a sitting judge
facts.quote: "No permission shall be granted for any public gathering or march that aims to personally target, defame or intimidate a sitting judge," the court said.

facts.claim: The court closed the petition after ruling that coordinated attacks against judges are not protected by constitutional free speech
facts.quote: The bench added that while citizens have "an undeniable right" to disagree with a judgement, coordinated attacks against judges are not protected by the constitutional right to free speech.

ai.background_note: The court's order addresses protests against a Supreme Court ruling on religious conversion and reservations, which were organized by groups like Tamil Nadu Thowheed Jamaath and Tamil Nadu Muslim Munnetra Kazhagam.
